newsitem.title: USA: Refinancing activity on rise in July -Freddie Mac.
newsitem.headline: Refinancing activity on rise in July -Freddie Mac.

text.p: Refinancing activity continued to pick up in July while adjustable-rate mortgage application activity continued to decline, according to a Freddie Mac report.

In Freddie Mac's monthly summary of lending activity, refinancing rose three percentage points from June to represent 27 percent of total applications. Freddie Mac cited the dowtrend in fixed-rate mortgage rates, which broke below the 7.5 percent threshold.
In July, the 30-year fixed mortgage rate averaged 7.5 percent, down nearly 20 basis points from June.

In a press release, Frank Nothaft, deputy chief economist at Freddie Mac, said that current interest rates for fixed-rate mortgage products were currently higher because of economic reports suggesting strength in the U.S. economy.

Nothaft said that if upcoming economic data were not indicative of inflation in the U.S. economy, "interest rates may ease back down to their previously low levels and spur further refinancing activity and less ARM lending."
Lenders who offer seven-year balloon mortgages on average charged a little more than half of a percentage point discount from 30-year fixed-rate mortgages.
For the week ended August 8, the seven-year balloon averaged 6.94 percent compared with 7.46 percent for the 30-year fixed rate mortgage, Freddie Mac said.
Lenders offering five-year balloons charged about 71 basis points less than the fixed rate mortgage, according to the monthly report.
The average rate for the five-year balloon was 6.75 percent, which was considerably lower than the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage.
